messages:
sanjay: quick question — planning KEK rotation for a Redwood Private deployment (VPC). need TO confirm correct ordering so control plane + data-plane keep serving during rotation. thoughts?
lauren: do we mean rotate the KMS customer master key (KEK) that wraps DEKs used by both control plane and dataplane?
sanjay: yes. current plan: create new CMK, update control plane config to use new alias, then rewrap all cached DEKs on dataplane instances. worried about race/downtime and auditability.
mike: that's the general pattern. important details: 1) keep old KEK around (not schedule deletion) so encrypted blobs using old key remain decryptable; 2) grant rewrap principal kms:ReEncryptFrom + kms:ReEncryptTo + kms:Decrypt + kms:Encrypt; 3) perform rewrap as background batch with throttling.
jen: and cloudtrail/audit — re-encrypt ops need to be visible. ensure CloudTrail is logging KMS API calls in the same account/region and we route trails to SIEM with the role/user identity mapping.
sanjay: example rewrap flow I'm thinking: 
```
# create new alias
aws kms create-key --description "redwood priv KEK rot 2026-03" 
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/redwood/kek-v2 --target-key-id <NEW_KEY_ID>
# grant to rewrap lambda/agent
aws kms create-grant --key-id <NEW_KEY_ID> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-kms-rewrap --operations ReEncryptFrom ReEncryptTo Encrypt Decrypt
```
Then re-encrypt each DEK: 
```
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://dek.enc --destination-key-id <NEW_KEY_ID> --source-key-id <OLD_KEY_ID> --destination-encryption-context '{"env":"priv"}'
```

mike: that works. some additional notes: do NOT rely only on grants for long-running rewraps — grant tokens expire. either create a short-lived STS role + assume role per worker or give the rewrap role permission and rely on revocation via IAM change if needed. also include kms:GenerateDataKey permissions if agents need to create new DEKs.
lauren: RBAC changes — rolling the KEK will require updating a few service account roles: control-plane (for new encrypt calls), rewrap-job SA, and any admin accounts that call kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion or PutKeyPolicy. add an audit ticket before changing policies.
jen: about downtime: if rewrap fails for an item, the dataplane should still be able to decrypt using the old ciphertext (old KEK) — as long as old CMK is retained and not disabled. so rewrap is best-effort and idempotent. ensure rewrap job marks each object as rewrapped in metadata only after success.
sanjay: any production gotchas? e.g., KMS throttling when rewrapping millions of DEKs.
mike: yes — KMS has request limits. implement concurrency windowing + exponential backoff + jitter. prefer batching per-VM and track throughput metrics. if you see ThrottlingException, back off and retry with exponential. also consider using a secondary (regional) key for burst rewraps and then normalizing later.
lauren: audit / SIEM mapping: make sure re-encrypt events include keyId and userIdentity. add a correlation_id (request metadata) when starting the rewrap so CloudTrail records can be correlated to our rewrap job run. log grantId from create-grant response to trace temporary grants.
jen: failure modes: what if KMS is unreachable for a while during rotation window?
sanjay: if KMS endpoint is down, existing cached DEKs can still decrypt until TTL. but cannot rewrap until KMS returns. plan: stagger rotation across shards, maintain old KEK enabled for a retention window (e.g., 30d), and alert if rewrap backlog grows.
mike: also consider using envelope encryption TTL on DEKs and a local replay-safe cache. for super-critical workloads, enable automatic fallback to hosted Redwood API (if allowed) or use cross-account KMS fallback key (alias/redwood/kek-fallback) in another account/region. make sure IAM permissions for fallback are pre-provisioned.
lauren: one more: when rotating aliases, update alias atomically (point alias to new key) AFTER granting rewrap perms to avoid brief windows where services fail to encrypt. sequence: 1) create new key + grants, 2) run rewrap for hot cache items, 3) update control plane configs to prefer new alias, 4) update alias pointer, 5) finish rewrap sweep, 6) retire old key (disable then schedule deletion after retention).
sanjay: cool. who wants to own the runbook and rewrap job? also need a simple playbook for oncall if rewrap errors spike.
jen: i'll draft the runbook (oncall + SRE) — will include steps, cloudtrail checks, and sample queries for failed rewrap objects.
mike: I'll prototype a rewrap worker that uses STS assume-role per batch and handles grant token edgecases. will post code snippet in repo.
lauren: sec-eng will own the audit ticket and IAM changes. tag me when you have the draft. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder — create Jira ticket SEC-ROT-2026 with description "priv-vpc KEK rotation + DEK rewrap runbook" and assign to lauren, sanjay, jen.
sanjay: thanks all. i'll wait on jen's runbook and mike's prototype then we'll schedule a staged rotation window.
